rationale: A unanimous, relatively narrow opinion is most likely, rejecting any categorical “background circumstances” requirement as inconsistent with Title VII’s “any individual” text and with McDonnell Douglas/Burdine’s low prima facie threshold. Roberts or Kagan are the most natural authors to produce a consensus, with separate concurrences most likely from Thomas/Gorsuch (textualist/separation-of-powers emphasis) or Alito (symmetry and administrability).
